newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Plessey down at start after earnings' fall.
newsitem.headline: Plessey down at start after earnings' fall.

text.p: Shares in South African telecommunications and electrical firm Plessey Corp Ltd slid at the start of trade on Friday following a fall in year results.
By 0740 GMT Plessey shares were down 50 cents or 5.7 percent to 850 cents in volume of 12,000 shares.
"It must be the results," a Johannesburg Stock Exchange dealer said.
"Although things are looking better for them for the new (financial year), the results were taken as pretty negative in the market," he said.
Plessey late on Thursday reported a fall in diluted earnings per share for the year ended March to 28.0 cents a share from 40.6 cents before. However, the dividend was held steady at 13.0 cents.
The group late last month sold off its loss-making consumer electronics division to Omega Holdings Ltd for 75 million rand.
Plessey said on Thursday that following the sale it was confident that its other operations would be able to restore profitability to satisfying levels.
